why:
Tier-1: docs only — one in-place update to docs/claude/health-review-backlog.json, and the row stays OPEN. No src/, no config/, no deploy/, no scripts/, no workflows. Not landing machinery, so R12 does not apply.

It records a MEASURED REFUTATION of the obvious remedy for the fixed-in-fact / open-on-paper class: a detector asking whether a landed change CITES a row id fires on 82 of 162 open high/critical rows, 50.6%, once the filing commit is excluded. A detector firing on half its population is the desensitised alarm, not a signal. Three of the 82 were verified fixed-in-fact this session and the other 79 are ungraded, so no precision figure is claimed — the denominator is the finding.

The weaker probe is recorded too: does a file the row names change after the row opened is 27 of 162, and is worse, because files move for every reason and it misses a fix that landed elsewhere.

Recording a refuted remedy IS the deliverable. The next session to pick that row would otherwise spend its time building the thing just measured not to work, which is the same failure the row is about one level up. It also independently supports the mi279 lane's measured guidance on its own class map: do not widen the patterns, precision is the weak axis.
